chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan from Zur'a from Sama'a from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

You say while you are at the door of the mosque: In the name of Allah and by Allah and from Allah and to Allah and whatever Allah willed, and upon the creed of the Messenger of Allah, and the best of names is for Allah, and praise is to Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon Muhammad ibn Abdullah, peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings, peace be upon the prophets of Allah and His messengers, peace be upon Ibrahim, the friend of the Merciful.
Peace be upon the messengers, and praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and have mercy on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers and blessed and had mercy on Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.

O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad Your servant and Your Messenger, and upon Ibrahim Your friend, and upon Your prophets and Your messengers, and grant them peace, and peace be upon the messengers, and praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy, and employ me in Your obedience and Your pleasure, and protect me with the protection of faith forever as long as You keep me alive. Exalted is the praise of Your Face, and praise to Allah who made me among His guests and visitors, and made me among those who build His mosques, and made me among those who converse with Him.

O Allah, indeed I am Your servant and Your visitor, and in Your house, and upon every visitor is a right for whoever visits him, and You are the best of visitors and the most noble of those visited, so I ask You, O Allah, O Merciful.

And by the fact that You are Allah, there is no god but You alone, no partner for You, and by the fact that You are One, Eternal, He neither begot nor was begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.

And that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family. O Generous, O Noble, O Compeller, O Kind, I ask You to make Your gift to me from my visiting You, that You grant me the ransom of my neck from the Fire.

O Allah, free my neck from the Fire. You say this three times, and expand for me from Your lawful and pure provision, and avert from me the evil of the devils of jinn and humans, and the evil of the transgressors of Arabs and non-Arabs.

key_terms.خَلِيلِ الرَّحْمَنِ: Friend of the Merciful (referring to Ibrahim)
key_terms.فَكَكَ رَقَبَتِي: Ransom of my neck (freedom from hellfire)
key_terms.مِلَّةِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Creed/religion of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite at the door of the mosque during pilgrimage?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this supplication serves as the formal entry ritual (dua al-dukhul) for the pilgrim at the threshold of the Sacred Mosque, emphasizing the transition from the mundane to the sacred space. It structurally mirrors the liturgical flow of the prayer, integrating the *Tawhid* of Surah Ikhlas with the *Hamd* of Surah Fatiha to affirm Allah’s oneness and gratitude before seeking intercession through the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt. The inclusion of specific petitions for protection from the 'corruptors of Arabs and Persians' reflects the historical context of early Shia communities navigating political and religious challenges during the pilgrimage season.
